title: Aquastat Failure
fullDescription: Honeywell aquastat relay controls residential oil/gas boilers. F01 (or 'F-01' on display) means internal CPU detected sensor or relay fault.

fixSteps.title: Reset aquastat
fixSteps.instruction: Press reset button on aquastat front cover.

fixSteps.title: Check sensor wiring
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect strap-on sensor wires - common point of corrosion.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.
safetyWarning: Boiler controls run on 120VAC. Power off at switch before opening.

title: Burner Lockout
shortDescription: S8600/S8610 ignition module locked out after failed trials.
fullDescription: Honeywell ignition modules try ignition 3 times. After failure, hard lockout requires manual reset and indicates flame proving issue.

fixSteps.title: Clean flame sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Steel wool or fine emery cloth on flame rod.

fixSteps.title: Reset module
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle thermostat or power for 60 seconds.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Pilot Outage Lockout
shortDescription: Honeywell SmartValve flashes slow - pilot won't stay lit.
fullDescription: SmartValve VR8345/8204 integrates ignition. Slow flash = pilot failed to prove flame within trial.

causes.cause: Air in gas line after service

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Internal Valve Failure
fullDescription: Steady (not blinking) LED means hardware fault inside the integrated valve. Replacement only.

fixSteps.title: Replace valve
fixSteps.instruction: SmartValve must be replaced as a unit; pro install.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Sensor Fault
shortDescription: L7224U detected sensor open or shorted.
fullDescription: Strap-on or immersion sensor reading outside expected resistance curve. Disables modulation, may force fixed setpoint.
symptoms: Boiler runs to high limit only

fixSteps.title: Inspect sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Replace cable ties, check for chafing.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Low Limit Sensor Fault
shortDescription: Aquastat low-limit input out of range.
fullDescription: Tankless coil systems use low-limit to maintain DHW temperature. Fault disables hot water priority.

fixSteps.title: Replace low-limit sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Drain partial, swap sensor, refill and bleed.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Manual Reset Required
shortDescription: Hard lockout from high limit or repeated trials.
fullDescription: Aquastat keeps lockout count - must press reset button after addressing root cause.

fixSteps.title: Press reset once
fixSteps.instruction: Press reset only once. Repeated resets without diagnosis is dangerous.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.
safetyWarning: Do not repeatedly reset - unburned gas can accumulate.

title: Communication Fault
shortDescription: EnviraCOM accessory lost link with control.
fullDescription: EnviraCOM is Honeywell's 2-wire control bus for outdoor reset modules and zone controls.

fixSteps.title: Check 1-2 polarity
fixSteps.instruction: EnviraCOM is polarity-sensitive. Verify 1 and 2 match at both ends.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: SmartValve Pressure Switch
fullDescription: Fast LED flash on SmartValve = vent pressure switch did not close. Common with blocked vent or weak inducer.

fixSteps.title: Inspect vent termination
fixSteps.instruction: Check for snow, leaves, bird nests at vent cap.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: Heat Anticipator Mismatch
fullDescription: Mechanical T87 thermostats need anticipator set to gas-valve current draw. Wrong setting causes overshoot or short cycles.

fixSteps.title: Measure valve current
fixSteps.instruction: Clamp meter on R wire while heating. Set anticipator pointer to that value.

whenToCallPro: When in doubt, call a pro.

title: T775 Sensor Open Circuit
shortDescription: Honeywell T775 series sensor reads open.
fullDescription:
On boiler controls using a Honeywell T775 strap-on or immersion sensor, an open-circuit reading prevents the controller from staging the boiler.

Reseat the sensor leads at the controller and verify continuity. Replace the sensor if needed.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wires
fixSteps.instruction: Open the controller and verify sensor leads are firmly landed.

fixSteps.title: Test Sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect at controller and measure across sensor element.

whenToCallPro: If sensor measures within spec but the controller still reads open, the controller input is faulty — replace controller via a technician.

title: T775 Sensor Short Circuit
fullDescription: Counterpart to T775-Open: a short on the sensor input. Common when the sensor is exposed to moisture or the leads are pinched.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Wires
fixSteps.instruction: Look for chafing on sensor leads.

whenToCallPro: Persistent short after sensor replacement = harness damage; call a technician.

title: L4006 Aquastat Trip
fullDescription:
Honeywell L4006 high-limit aquastat opens when boiler water exceeds the dial set point (typically 200-220 F). The boiler cannot fire until the water cools and the limit closes — or, if equipped with manual reset, until the button is pressed.

Frequent trips suggest a stuck circulator, scaled heat exchanger, or set point too low.

fixSteps.title: Allow Cool Down
fixSteps.instruction: Let the system cool below limit.

fixSteps.title: Check Pump
fixSteps.instruction: Verify circulator runs on call for heat.

fixSteps.title: Press Manual Reset
fixSteps.instruction: If equipped, press the reset button.

fixSteps.title: Verify Set Point
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm dial is at correct temperature.

whenToCallPro: If pump is healthy and limit trips repeatedly, call a heating technician.

title: L4007 Low-Limit Failure
fullDescription:
The L4007 (and similar) low-limit circulator controls hold the boiler at a minimum temperature for tankless coil DHW. A failed L4007 may keep the burner on continuously or refuse to call the burner.

Replace the control if dial response is incorrect after verifying wiring.
symptoms: Burner runs continuously or never starts
whenToCallPro: Aquastat replacement on older boilers should be done by a qualified technician.

title: Honeywell EnviraCom Communication Loss
fullDescription: Code EC1 (EnviraCom) on Honeywell-controlled boilers indicates the EnviraCom bus between control and devices (zone valves, thermostats) is not communicating. Check the 2-wire EnviraCom run.
whenToCallPro: If wiring is intact, replace the master controller via a technician.

title: EnviraCom Address Conflict
shortDescription: Two devices share the same EnviraCom address.
fullDescription: Code EC2 means two devices on the EnviraCom bus have the same address. Each device must have a unique address; consult the device manuals.

fixSteps.title: Identify Devices
fixSteps.instruction: List all EnviraCom devices and their addresses.

fixSteps.title: Reassign
fixSteps.instruction: Set each to a unique address.

whenToCallPro: If addressing is correct but EC2 returns, a device may be defective — call a technician.

title: EnviraCom Power Fault
shortDescription: EnviraCom bus power out of range.
fullDescription: Code EC3 indicates the bus voltage is too high or too low. Typical causes are a shorted device pulling voltage down or a wiring error.

fixSteps.title: Disconnect Devices
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect each device until the fault clears to identify the offender.

whenToCallPro: If isolation does not identify the cause, call a technician.

title: Honeywell SmartValve Lockout
fullDescription: On boilers with Honeywell SmartValve (SV9501/SV9540 series), a hard lockout indicates the valve detected a flame fault, ignition failure, or internal error. Reset by cycling thermostat call; if it returns, diagnose flame rod, gas pressure, and venting.

fixSteps.title: Reset
fixSteps.instruction: Cycle thermostat call off then on.

whenToCallPro: SmartValve diagnosis and replacement should be done by a qualified technician.

title: Honeywell Pilot Sensing Fault
shortDescription: Pilot flame sensing weak or lost.
fullDescription: Code EC5 indicates the pilot flame is sensed weakly or intermittently — typically caused by a fouled thermocouple/thermopile or a pilot orifice partially clogged.

fixSteps.title: Inspect Pilot
fixSteps.instruction: Visually verify a strong blue pilot.

fixSteps.title: Clean Pilot
fixSteps.instruction: Clear the pilot orifice with compressed air.

whenToCallPro: If the pilot is weak after cleaning, gas pressure may be marginal — call a technician.

title: Honeywell Pump Logic Fault
shortDescription: Pump-logic relay output stuck or failed.
fullDescription: Code EC6 (also seen on RM7800/RM7895 controls) indicates the pump-logic relay output is stuck or showing feedback inconsistent with the commanded state. Replace the control if the feedback circuit is internally damaged.
symptoms: Pump runs unexpectedly or not at all
whenToCallPro: Stuck pump-logic relays require control replacement by a technician.
